title: Examining the Role of Sensitivity to Uncertain Threat and Alcohol Response in Risk for Alcohol Use Disorder Following Sexual Assault in College Women
official: Examining the Role of Sensitivity to Uncertain Threat and Alcohol Response in Risk for Alcohol Use Disorder Following Sexual Assault in College Women
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether women who engage in heavy drinking with a history of sexual assault (SA) victimization show heightened baseline reactivity to uncertain threat (U-threat), whether alcohol reduces this reactivity and related anxiety, and how these processes link to real-world drinking behavior. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Test whether heavy drinking women with a history of SA display exaggerated baseline reactivity to U-threat.
* In the lab, test whether alcohol intoxication is associated with decreases in reactivity to U-threat and subjective anxiety, particularly in heavy drinking women with a history of SA.
* In the real-world, test associations between SA victimization, reactivity to U-threat, alcohol consumption, and anxiolytic relief.

Participants will:

* Complete a screening and orientation session
* Complete two experimental lab sessions that will include intravenous (IV) administration of either 80mg% alcohol or placebo (saline), order counterbalanced
* Complete daily ecological momentary assessments (EMA) surveys for 21 days
* Wear a transdermal alcohol wrist biosensor (BACTrack Skyn) for 21-days
criteria:
General Inclusion Criteria for All Participants:

* Biological female
* 21-29 years old
* At least a high school education
* Fluency in English
* Heavy drinker as defined as 8 or more alcoholic drinks per week and at least two binge episodes (4 or more drinks for in a 2-hour period) in the past month

Additional Inclusion Criteria for Heavy Drinkers with History of Sexual Assault (HD+SA) Group:

\- Self-reported experience of sexual assault victimization after age 14.

Additional Inclusion Criteria for Heavy Drinkers without History of Sexual Assault (HD-SA) Group:

\- No exposure to lifetime DSM-5 Criterion A traumatic stressor. Participants will not be excluded for accidents, injuries, or witnessing community violence to ensure the sample is representative.

Exclusion Criteria for All Participants:

* Any serious medical problems (e.g., liver disease, cardiac abnormality, pancreatitis, diabetes, neurological problems, and gastrointestinal disorders)
* Body weight \< 110 or \> 210 lbs
* Current medical or psychiatric condition requiring medication for which alcohol consumption is contraindicated
* Substance use disorder other than mild and moderate alcohol use disorder
* Positive urine screen for drugs other than cannabis
* Currently seeking or past-12-month history of inpatient or intensive treatment for addictive behaviors
* Pregnancy, nursing, or planning to become pregnant in the next 3 months
* Report smoking more than 5 cigarettes (or electronic equivalent) per day
* Lifetime history of psychosis.

Additional Exclusion Criteria for HD+SA Group:

\- Report a first onset SA within the past 30 days
